title: Industrial Policy Delivers A Fiscal Payoff
gist: Gavekal argues that China's 2026 wave of blockbuster tech IPOs is turning local governments' long-standing venture-capital stakes into large paper gains, transforming the finances of successful governments. Examples: Beijing, Shenzhen and Shanghai stakes in Unitree Robotics worth about RMB14bn after its August IPO, and five provincial-level backers of display maker HKC holding about RMB37bn after its June listing.

themes.theme: State VC exits via China's IPO wave

insights.claim: China's string of blockbuster IPOs in 2026 has created enormous paper wealth for some local governments, which are significant shareholders in the latest generation of Chinese technology companies.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: China's IPO pipeline now has a fiscal constituency: local governments benefit directly from open listing windows, which makes continued policy support for tech IPOs more likely.
insights.quote: This year’s string of blockbuster IPOs in China has created enormous paper wealth for some local governments

insights.claim: Government entities have dominated venture-capital investing in China for years, and the difference now is that more of their portfolio companies are going public, so more of those state investments are actually paying off.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The exit channel for state VC is reopening, which recycles capital into new state-backed tech bets. Watch IPO approval pace as the swing variable for Chinese venture funding.

themes.theme: Equity stakes as local fiscal assets

insights.claim: Chinese local authorities have long used equity investments as a tool of industrial policy and economic development. As financial gains become more common, the finances of the governments that picked winners are also being transformed.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Local government balance sheets will diverge by skill at picking winners. Tech-hub cities with successful portfolios gain fiscal room while land-sale-dependent peers stay constrained, which matters for LGFV credit differentiation.
insights.quote: with financial gains becoming more common, the finances of successful governments are also being transformed

insights.claim: Industrial policy in China is producing a direct fiscal payoff: local governments' equity stakes in newly listed tech firms are emerging as a new source of government wealth, not just a development tool.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: This challenges the view that Chinese industrial policy is only a fiscal drain. Mark-to-market gains on listed stakes could partly offset weak land revenue for the winning jurisdictions.

insights.claim: The Beijing, Shenzhen and Shanghai governments all invested in Unitree Robotics, and after its August 2026 IPO their combined stakes are worth about RMB14bn.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Large state holdings in Unitree are a future supply overhang once lock-ups expire. They also mean local governments have a stake in robotics-sector valuations staying high.

insights.claim: Display maker HKC, which went public in June 2026, has multiple local-government backers from Chongqing, Sichuan, Guizhou, Hunan and Anhui, whose combined stakes are worth about RMB37bn.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Inland provinces co-funding display capacity now hold sizable listed equity. Watch for stake sales after lock-ups and for these gains being used to shore up provincial finances.
